assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, the micro-founded policy model and the rule-based view of monetary policy is the working basis of modern central banking and policy analysis. Its influence on both theory and practice is very large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many contributors (Calvo pricing, Taylor rule, Woodford's integrated framework, Gali's empirical and theoretical work, Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans medium-scale models, Smets-Wouters estimation). Woodford (unified framework), Gali (theory and evidence) and Taylor (policy rule) cover the conceptual, empirical and policy-rule contributions, but the omission of Calvo, Gertler and the Christiano-Eichenbaum group is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: Developed from the 1980s to the 2000s and tested through several decades of policy use, including the financial crisis, the post-pandemic inflation episode and the zero-lower-bound period. Fully mature.
uncertainties: Attribution among eight listed names is contested and a three-person split is somewhat arbitrary.
Criticism of the framework after the financial crisis and the 2021-23 inflation could weigh against it, while heterogeneous-agent extensions may be seen as the successor.
I cannot independently verify the exact origin of each contribution from the supplied evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run series on top income and wealth shares, built from tax and administrative data, changed both the research agenda and public debate on inequality. The data infrastructure (the World Inequality Database lineage) is a durable public good. The offshore wealth estimates add a distinct contribution.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the core of the top-income-share work, and Zucman is the main figure on offshore wealth and wealth distribution. The three-person grouping is coherent. Atkinson, who is deceased, was a precursor and cannot be credited.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work dates from the early 2000s and has been replicated and extended internationally. The wealth and offshore work is more recent and is still being debated.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over wealth-share measurement and capitalization methods remain.
Piketty's theoretical claims about r > g are contested, and the committee may prefer credit for measurement rather than theory.
Public and policy advocacy could complicate how the award is seen.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Credible empirical evidence on how import competition and technology reshape local labour markets, wages and employment. It changed how economists and policymakers think about the distributional costs of trade, and it shows the credibility-revolution toolkit applied to a first-order question.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock work is primarily Autor-Dorn-Hanson. Autor's earlier task-based work, with Katz and others, is a separate strand with a wider group of contributors, so the proposed trio concentrates on the trade-shock contribution. Katz is an omitted but plausible alternative.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from about 2013-2016, and the follow-up literature has now spanned a decade, with some replication and reinterpretation.
uncertainties: Debate continues on the size and persistence of the shock effects and on the identification and shift-share designs.
Task-based technology credit is split among several people, including Acemoglu, who is already a laureate.
It is unclear whether the committee views the work as mainly an empirical finding or as a conceptual innovation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade model recast international trade around firm selection, productivity differences and new channels for gains from trade. It spawned a large body of theory and firm-level empirical work and shaped trade policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central source. Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple extend it to exporting versus FDI, and Helpman's wider contributions cover firm heterogeneity and labour markets. Redding is influential on quantitative applications, but the two-person group best reflects the core. Krugman's earlier prize covers the preceding wave of new trade theory.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of use, with extensive empirical testing and quantitative extensions. Mature.
uncertainties: Close precedents (Eaton-Kortum, Bernard-Jensen empirical work) complicate attribution.
Helpman also appears in a separate political-economy trade candidate, so credit overlaps across ballot entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit cycles explain how small shocks are amplified and persist through balance sheets. The framework is a foundation of macro-finance and of post-2008 policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is the central model. Gertler contributed to the financial accelerator with Bernanke (a prior laureate, recognised for banking crises) and to later work on intermediation. Gilchrist is an empirical contributor but not core to the theory.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work is nearly three decades old, and its relevance was confirmed in the 2008 crisis and later.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist accelerator and with the Diamond-Dybvig and Bernanke prizes may prompt the committee to think the area is already recognised.
Gertler also appears in the New Keynesian candidate, so credit overlaps across entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data used to measure intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the causal role of place. It is methodologically and substantively influential, and in my own field it builds on the same register-data approach.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are the main figures on causal neighbourhood effects and mobility, and Chetty leads the broader Opportunity Insights programme. Friedman and Katz are significant co-authors. Chetty's work is also credited under other candidates, so attributing this entry to a specific contribution is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The main papers date from 2014-2018 and later. Replications and related international register studies are accumulating, but the long-term policy lessons are still developing.
uncertainties: The work may be seen as too recent relative to typical prize timing.
Large team science makes it hard to decide how many names to include.
Whether the neighbourhood-effect estimates remain robust under further scrutiny is not yet settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Formal and empirical analysis of how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It created modern political economics as a field and links institutions to policy outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the authors of the main synthesis and of the constitutional and electoral-rule work. Besley contributes accountability and state-capacity themes. Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson received the 2024 prize on institutions, which overlaps with part of this area.
assessment.maturity: Established since the 1990s, with a large body of follow-on work. Mature.
uncertainties: The 2024 institutions prize may reduce room for another award in a neighbouring area.
Persson's affiliation with Stockholm is a conflict-type factor that I note and do not adjudicate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A measurement framework for how misallocation of inputs across firms explains cross-country differences in productivity and income. It linked micro data to aggregate development outcomes and generated a large literature.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the core paper and the two are its principal authors. Restuccia and Rogerson developed a closely related strand, so the exclusion of Restuccia is a real attribution risk.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of use with extensive applications. The concept is established, though its measurement is still debated.
uncertainties: Measurement concerns about whether dispersion in marginal products reflects true misallocation or measurement error and adjustment costs.
The credit split with Restuccia and Rogerson is unresolved, and Rogerson is not on the list.
